why: capabilities.json records retirement in the free-text `notes` field, but a routing policy that never reads notes will happily keep selecting a retired model: the live ones still answer, so every availability check passes.

Retirement is a human judgement, not something to auto-derive, so this file is hand-curated from the `notes` evidence rather than generated. `tools/build-capabilities.mjs` prints the candidates it found for review; it deliberately does not write them.

A model absent from this file is treated as `active`, so adding an entry is the only way to retire one. The status is per ROUTE as configured here: a model whose free tier is retired is retired for routing even if the weights remain published.

statuses.deprecated: Vendor has retired this endpoint. Never route to it.
